CSE_3.subject: Data Structure and Algorithms

courseOutcomes.description: Analyze the time and space complexity of simple algorithms and code segments using asymptotic notations.
Choose among the fundamental data structures and apply them to solve computational problems.
Choose the efficient searching and sorting algorithms and apply them for problem solving.
Apply tree and graph for problem solving.
Evaluate the performance of advanced data structures such as heaps, priority queues, and hash tables for problem solving, enhancing data storage and retrieval efficiency.

modules.title: Module 1: Introduction
topics: The notion of data structures and algorithms

modules.title: Module 2: Fundamental Data Structures
topics: Stacks and queues and their implementations using arrays and linked lists
Uses of stacks and queues in expression evaluation and conversion

modules.title: Module 3: Searching and Sorting
topics: Merge sort with average- and worst-case analysis
Quick sort with average- and worst-case analysis
Choosing better data structures for different kinds of search and sort

modules.title: Module 4: Trees and Graphs
topics: Basic definitions of graph and tree
Graph representation: adjacency list and adjacency matrix

modules.title: Module 5: Advanced Trees
topics: Binary Search Trees: definition and basic algorithms
Informal discussion of extension to B-trees

modules.title: Module 6: Heaps and Priority Queues
topics: Priority Queue ADT and basic implementation methods
Implementation of priority queues using heaps and running-time analysis

textbooks: Expert Data Structures with C — R.B. Patel, Khanna Book Publishing Company, New Delhi, 4th Edition
Fundamentals of Data Structures, Illustrated Edition — Ellis Horowitz and Sartaj Sahni, Computer Science Press
Introduction to Algorithms — Cormen et al.

CSE_3.subject: Object Oriented Programming

courseOutcomes.description: Demonstrate proficiency in using programming environments, debugging tools, and source code management systems for efficient software development and maintenance.
Apply object-oriented programming (OOP) principles to design maintainable and well-structured software solutions.
Implement advanced OOP features in C++ and Java to develop scalable and efficient applications.
Develop robust software using unit testing frameworks and defensive programming techniques to ensure reliability and error handling.
Create software architectures using software modeling techniques and design patterns such as class diagrams and sequence diagrams.

modules.title: Module 2: Object-Oriented Paradigm
topics: Identifying classes, attributes, methods and objects

modules.title: Module 7: Data Structure and Algorithms Laboratory

textbooks: Object-Oriented Analysis and Design with Applications — Grady Booch et al.
Programming Language Pragmatics, 4th Edition — M. Scott

The Unified Modeling Language Reference Manual — J. Rumbaugh et al.

CSE_3.subject: Software Engineering

courseOutcomes.description: Select the most appropriate software process models for a given project scenario.
Apply project estimation and risk management techniques to plan, schedule, and manage software projects efficiently.

Develop a comprehensive Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document based on requirement engineering principles, design efficient software architectures using appropriate design methodologies and propose coding styles.
Evaluate software quality through testing techniques and SQA practices to ensure reliability and maintainability of software systems.
Apply modern Computer Aided Software Engineering (CASE) tools in the software life cycle to improve process automation and software quality.

modules.title: Module 1: Introduction and Software Process Models
Module 2: Software Project Management
topics: Role of management in software development

modules.title: Module 5: Testing and Software Quality
topics: Unit, integration, system and regression testing

modules.title: Module 6: CASE and Advanced Topics
topics: Computer Aided Software Engineering (CASE) and its scope
CASE support in software life cycle
Software engineering challenges of Big Data

textbooks: Software Engineering: A Practitioner’s Approach — R.S. Pressman, 3rd Edition (as printed in syllabus)
Software Engineering — Ian Sommerville, Pearson Education Asia, 6th Edition, 2000
An Integrated Approach to Software Engineering — Pankaj Jalote, Springer Verlag, 1997
Software Engineering: An Engineering Approach — James F. Peters and Witold Pedryez, John Wiley and Sons

CSE_3.subject: Digital Systems

courseOutcomes.description: Demonstrate familiarity with the fundamentals of digital systems to analyze and implement basic digital circuits.
Analyze and construct combinational digital circuits.
Analyze and construct sequential digital circuits.
Apply A/D and D/A conversion techniques in digital systems.
Design and differentiate memory architectures and programmable logic devices for efficient digital system design.

modules.title: Module 1: Digital Fundamentals
topics: AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR and Exclusive-OR operations
Binary, signed binary, octal and hexadecimal number systems
TTL, Schottky TTL and CMOS logic
Representation of floating-point numbers in IEEE 754 standards

modules.title: Module 2: Combinational Logic
topics: Simplification of logic functions using K-map

Digital Logic and Computer Design — M.M. Mano, Pearson Education India, 2016
Fundamentals of Digital Circuits — A. Kumar, Prentice Hall India, 2016

CSE_3.subject: Mathematics III-D

courseOutcomes.description: Apply knowledge of algebraic structures to understand the basics of the theoretical foundation of computer science.
Apply the basic principles of probability and probability distributions in the context of data science.
Analyse and draw conclusions from sample data.
Apply graph-theoretic techniques to solve problems of Computer Science and Engineering.

modules.title: Module 1: Algebraic Structures
topics: Definitions and basic properties of semigroups, monoids and groups
Basics of rings, integral domains and fields
Introduction to lattices and Boolean algebras

modules.title: Module 2: Probability and Random Variables
topics: Cumulative distribution function and its properties
Discrete, continuous and mixed random variables
Binomial, Poisson, uniform and normal distributions

modules.title: Module 3: Statistical Inference
topics: Tests of significance for large and small samples

modules.title: Module 4: Graph Theory
topics: Graphs and their representations by adjacency and incidence matrices

textbooks: Discrete Mathematical Structures with Application to Computer Science — J.P. Trembly and R.P. Manohar, Tata McGraw Hill, 2001

Statistical Methods: An Introductory Text — J. Medhi, New Age International Publishers

CSE_3.subject: Indian Knowledge Systems
courseObjectives: Introduce foundational concepts of Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS)
Explore contributions of ancient and medieval India in science, technology, mathematics and philosophy
Develop appreciation for traditional Indian knowledge and its relevance in modern contexts
Encourage critical thinking about indigenous knowledge systems and their applications

courseOutcomes.description: Understand the key principles of Indian Knowledge Systems.
Recognize India's contributions to science, mathematics, medicine and engineering.
Analyze the interdisciplinary nature of IKS and its connections with modern technology.
Appreciate the philosophical and ethical dimensions of traditional Indian knowledge.

modules.title: Module 1: Introduction to Indian Knowledge System (IKS)
topics: Definition, scope and significance of IKS
Sources of Indian knowledge: Vedas, Upanishads, Puranas, Smritis and other texts
Classification of knowledge in Indian tradition (Vidyas and Kalas)

modules.title: Module 2: Science and Technology in Ancient India
topics: Contributions to mathematics: zero, decimal system, Vedic Mathematics, Aryabhata and Brahmagupta
Astronomy and space science: Surya Siddhanta, planetary motion and concept of time
Metallurgy and material sciences: Iron Pillar, Wootz Steel and Ayurvedic alloys
Civil engineering and architecture: temple architecture, town planning and water management

modules.title: Module 3: Indian Philosophical and Ethical Systems
topics: Key schools of Indian philosophy: Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Samkhya, Yoga and Vedanta
Concept of Dharma, Karma and sustainable living
Ethics in science and technology from an Indian perspective

modules.title: Module 4: Traditional Medicine and Wellness Systems
topics: Foundations of Ayurveda, Yoga and Siddha
Relevance of traditional medicine in modern healthcare

modules.title: Module 5: IKS in Contemporary Applications
topics: Revival of traditional knowledge in modern science and engineering
Case studies such as Panchakarma in wellness technology and Vastu in architecture
Government initiatives: National Education Policy 2020 and IKS Division under AICTE

textbooks: Indian Knowledge Systems — Kapil Kapoor and Avadhesh Kumar Singh
Ancient Indian Leaps into Mathematics — B.S. Yadav
Science and Technology in Ancient India — O.P. Jaggi
The Positive Sciences of the Ancient Hindus — Brajendranath Seal
AICTE Model Curriculum for IKS

CSE_3.subject: Language other than MIL

courseOutcomes.description: Demonstrate understanding of basic grammar rules including subject-verb agreement, tenses and cases, and apply them in constructing grammatically correct sentences.
Identify and correct common grammatical and usage errors in written English.
Enhance vocabulary through synonyms, antonyms, idiomatic expressions and phrasal verbs.
Apply verbal reasoning skills to comprehend, arrange and complete sentences and paragraphs.
Develop reading comprehension skills using skimming, scanning and intensive reading.
Produce coherent and concise writing through precis writing and essay composition.

textbooks: Objective General English — S.P. Bakshi, Arihant Publication India Ltd., 2021
Descriptive English — S.P. Bakshi, Arihant Publication India Ltd., 2016

CSE_3.subject: Data Structure and Algorithms Lab

courseOutcomes.description: Analyze runtime of simple algorithms or code segments.
Implement linear and non-linear data structures such as arrays, stacks, queues and linked lists to solve computational problems.
Implement searching and sorting algorithms in terms of time and space complexity.
Implement trees and graphs and perform basic tree and graph traversals using suitable programs.
Choose and implement appropriate data structures for specific application scenarios.

experiments: Worst/average-case analysis and asymptotic notations for small pseudocodes
Different kinds of linked lists with all possible operations
Stacks and queues using linked lists and arrays
Bubble, insertion, selection, merge and quick sort using arrays; check possibility of implementing using linked lists
Binary search trees and basic tree traversal algorithms
Graph implementation using adjacency list and adjacency matrix
textbooks: Expert Data Structures with C — R.B. Patel, Khanna Book Publishing Company, New Delhi, 4th Edition
Fundamentals of Data Structures, Illustrated Edition — Ellis Horowitz and Sartaj Sahni, Computer Science Press
Data Structure Through C — Yashavant P. Kanetkar, BPB Publications

CSE_3.subject: Object Oriented Programming Lab

courseOutcomes.description: Implement classes and objects to encapsulate data and methods in C++ programs.
Implement C++ programs using OOP concepts such as inheritance, function overloading and operator overloading.
Implement programs demonstrating constructors, destructors and access specifiers for effective memory and access control.
Design and develop object-oriented solutions for real-life scenarios such as library management and banking systems.

experiments: Class with data members and member functions
Create multiple objects of a class and use their data members and member functions
Array of objects and use of data members and member functions
Classes and objects for real problems such as book shops, libraries and banks

CSE_3.subject: Python Programming Lab

courseOutcomes.description: Apply basic building blocks of Python programming.
Develop Python programs using control structures, functions and data structures to solve real-world problems.
Implement basic object-oriented programming concepts using Python programs.
Design and develop interactive graphical user interfaces using Python GUI libraries to create applications and simple games.

modules.title: Module 1: Python Fundamentals
topics: Importance of IDEs such as Spyder (Anaconda) and PyCharm
Python shell as a calculator and for direct expressions
Hello World program in Python script
Comparison, arithmetic, logical, Boolean, bitwise and assignment operators
Numbers, lists, tuples, strings, sets and dictionaries

modules.title: Module 2: Control Flow, Functions and Data Structures
topics: Problem solving using dictionaries as lookup tables

modules.title: Module 4: GUI Programming
topics: GUI creation using tkinter or alternatives such as wxPython, PyQt (PySide), Pygame, Pyglet and PyGTK
Labels, buttons, entry/textbox, combobox, checkbutton, radiobutton, scrolledText/textarea, spinbox, progressbar, menubar, filedialog and tabs
Simple GUI games such as Tic-Tac-Toe

textbooks: Think Python: How to Think Like a Computer Scientist, 2nd Edition — Allen B. Downey, O'Reilly, 2016
Learn Python 3 the Hard Way, 3rd Edition — Zed A. Shaw, Addison-Wesley, 2017
